page: Microsoft Azure F64als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated 64-core AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz with one thread per physical core, the instance allocates 128.0 GB of system RAM, establishing a compute-dense 2.0 GB of memory per core ratio. The instance includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains no dedicated GPUs and provisions no local disk storage, relying on external Premium Storage volumes for persistence.

Benchmark data reflects strong overall CPU capabilities, particularly under multi-threaded compute workloads. In stress-ng testing, the multi-core CPU benchmark placed in the top tier, matching the top-tier rankings recorded in PassMark CPU score and Geekbench multi-core evaluation. Compute-intensive operations demonstrate high throughput, with Clang software compilation, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and ray tracing all placing in the top 10 percent of recorded results. In-memory and cache-bound workloads also perform at an elevated tier, evidenced by Redis SET operations exceeding 135 million operations per second and cached memory bandwidth exceeding 9,200 GB/s.

The instance provides high computational density per resource unit by prioritizing physical CPU cores over auxiliary resources. However, the low memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU and the total absence of bundled local storage require architectural consideration for memory-hungry or IO-bound applications. The configuration is well suited for CPU-bound tasks such as code compilation pipelines, distributed batch compute, multi-threaded physics modeling, scientific simulations, and web-scale caching layers where execution speed is tied directly to dedicated x86 execution units rather than memory capacity.
description: The Microsoft Azure F64als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine driven by a 64-core AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with dedicated physical cores and single-threading, the instance provides 128.0 GB of RAM, offering a compact 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. It features advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via SHA-NI and VAES, though it contains no integrated GPUs and provisions no local disk storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier multi-threaded processing performance across Geekbench, PassMark, and stress-ng tests, alongside top-tier execution in Clang software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis SET throughput. The instance achieves high compute density and cost efficiency for compute-focused architectures, balanced against the constraint of low per-core memory capacity. It is primarily suited for large-scale software compilation, distributed batch processing, CPU-based scientific simulations, and high-throughput static web serving.
